findings.title: Plumbing installed; proper backflow devices.
findings.comment: Inspector observed the hand sink next to the dish area to have a gradual leak from the waste line. A plumber responded last week, but the leak persists. Ensure the plumber returns to repair the sink and all wastewater is surveyed properly to prevent cross-contamination. Inspector will follow up again on July 16, 2026.
findings.citation_text: 5-205.15(A) System Maintained in Good Repair. A plumbing system shall be: (A) Repaired according to LAW.

findings.title: Food separated and protected.
findings.comment: Inspector observed raw shell eggs stored above pots of soup in the walk-in cooler. Staff were informed and the eggs were moved to a shelf above raw chicken. Education was conducted with the PIC regarding proper storage order practices, and a handout in Chinese and English was provided. Ensure proper storage order is followed at all times to prevent cross-contamination.
findings.citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(1) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (1) Except as specified in (1)(d) below or when combined as ingredients, separating raw animal FOODS during storage, preparation, holding, and display from: (a) Raw READY-TO-EAT FOOD including other raw animal FOOD such as FISH for sushi or MOLLUSCAN SHELLFISH, or other raw READY-TOEAT FOOD such as fruits and vegetables, (b) Cooked READY-TO-EAT FOOD, and (c) Fruits and vegetables before they are washed; (d) Frozen, commercially processed and packaged raw animal FOOD may be stored or displayed with or above frozen, commercially processed and packaged, ready-to-eat food.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: Inspector observed the interior baffles of the ice machine as well as the counter surrounding the ice basin of the soda machine to be heavily soiled with microbial growth. The PIC was informed and plans to contact a service representative for professional cleaning. A follow-up will be conducted on July 20, 2026 to ensure the ice machine and ice basin of the soda machine is clean to sight and touch.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: Inspector observed the dish machine in the kitchen to measure 0ppm chlorine with a test strip. The PIC was informed and discovered that the bucket of chemical attached to the machine was empty. The bucket was replaced and the machine was cycled multiple times to prime the chemical. Chemical was not detected after multiple cycles. A follow up will be conducted on July 13, 2026.
findings.citation_text: 4-501.114(A) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (A) A chlorine solution shall have a minimum temperature based on the concentration and PH of the solution as listed in the chart in 4-501.114 (A).

findings.title: Plumbing installed; proper backflow devices.
findings.comment: Inspector observed a slow wastewater leak from the plumbing below the hand sink near the dish area. findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment: Inspector observed the triple sink and mop sink in the kitchen to have damaged silicone sealant between the sinks and the wall. The sealant was observed both cracked/damaged and soiled with microbial growth. Ensure staff remove the existing sealant and replace it with new silicone to make the surface smooth, nonabsorbent, and easily cleanable. This repair needs to be completed prior to the next routine inspection.

findings.title: Food separated and protected.
findings.comment:
2nd Repeat Violation

Inspector observed rice and rice noodles soaking in buckets with no lid stored directly on the floor. The PIC was advised to keep food containers covered at all times as well as at least 6 inches off the ground. Coverings help prevent contamination from dust, bacteria and other foods/equipment above the food container. The PIC placed covers on both buckets and moved them to a counter during the inspection. This violation is considered corrected on site. 

The inspector recommends investing in additional shelving or carts for buckets to avoid this violation in the future.

findings.title: Food separated and protected.
findings.comment:
The following food storage/contamination violations were observed in the kitchen: 
1. Rice and rice noodles soaking in water in buckets on the floor. Advised to store elsewhere on a shelf or table. Never store open containers of food on the floor to prevent contamination. Staff moved rice and noodles off floor.
2. Raw beef stored in the deli cooler above open container of cut iceberg lettuce. Advised that the juices from the beef could drip into the lettuce, resulting in contamination. Always store raw meat at the lowest shelf, and produce above. Storage order was fixed immediately.

findings.title: Time as a Public Health Control; procedures & records
findings.comment:
3-501.19: (A) If time without temperature used for public health control, written procedure approved by regulatory authority shall be available upon request (Pf). (B) If time is used as control for up to 4 hours, food shall have initial temperature of 41F (or less) or 135F (or greater). FOOD shall be marked, cooked and served within 4 hour time limit. If FOOD is unmarked or marked exceeding 4-hour limit, FOOD shall be discarded. (P) (C) If time is used as control for up to 6 hours, food shall have initial temperature of 41F or less. FOOD shall not exceed 70F. If FOOD is unmarked or marked exceeding 6-hour limit, FOOD shall be discarded. (D) HSP FOOD ESTABLISHMENTS cannot use time control for raw eggs. 

Time as a control policy written today as a flat of eggs is observed to be sitting out at room temperature. Cook says that the eggs need to be room temperature for proper cooking in dish. Time was written on egg flat. Eggs will be used or discarded by 2:30pm.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.comment:
6-301.12: Each HANDWASHING SINK shall be provided with: (A) Individual, disposable towels; (B) A continuous towel system that supplies the user with a clean towel; (C) A heated-air hand drying device; (D) A hand drying device that employs an air-knife system that delivers high velocity, pressurized air at ambient temperatures. 

Observed employee bathroom in the kitchen to lack paper towels. Ensure paper towels are at each hand washing sink. Discussed with PIC. Replaced with new paper towels. COS.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-501.114: Chemical sanitizer for manual or mechanical operation shall meet proper criteria: (A) chlorine shall have minimum temperature (55F), concentration (100ppm), and pH (10). (B) Iodine shall have 68F, pH of 5 or less and concentration of 12.5ppm and 25ppm. (C) Quaternary ammonium shall have 75F, concentration based on label, and water with 500ppm hardness or less. (D) - (E) Meets EPA-label use and regulatory authority approval. (P) (F) Other chemical sanitzers in-use shall have EPA-registered label, display device registration number on devide and is operated and maintained in accordance with manufacturers instructions (Pf)

Observed sanitization bucket in the kitchen to be low - 0 ppm. Bleach was added - 50 to 100 ppm. PIC tested with his own test strips. Discussed with PIC that sanitization buckets should be changed every 4-6 hours or sooner dependent on weakened concentration. COS.

findings.title: Thermometers provided & accurate
findings.comment:
4-204.112: (A) In refrigerated or hot FOOD storage unit, TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICE shall be located to measure air temperature. (B) EQUIPMENT holding TCS FOOD shall have TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICE affixed to device. (C) Does not apply to EQUIPMENT without practical means of measuring ambient air surroundings. (D) TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICES shall be designed to be easily readable. C (E) FOOD and water TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICES shall have numerical scale, printed record, or digital readout in increments no greater than 1C or 2F in the intended range of use. Pf

Observed no thermometers in the front cooler (bar prep cooler and reach-in cooler). Provide thermometers for these coolers before next routine inspection.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
4-601.11: (B) The FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of cooking EQUIPMENT and pans shall be kept free of encrusted grease deposits and other soil accumulations. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

(REPEAT) Observed the baffles to have an accumulation of grease debris. Steam Power currently comes twice a year. Suggested to PIC that company comes 3x yearly due to build-up presence. This is a repeat violation since the last routine inspection on 5/15/21.

findings.title: Management, food employee and conditional employee; knowledge, responsibilities and reporting
findings.comment:
2-201.11: (A) The PERMIT HOLDER shall require FOOD EMPLOYEES and CONDITIONAL EMPLOYEES to report to the PERSON IN CHARGE information about their health and activities as they relate to diseases that are transmissible through FOOD. Report: Symptoms (all P except lesion), diagnosis (all P), and possible exposures (P).  (E) Responsibility of food employee to report symptoms/disease to PIC. 

Observed no signed employee health reporting agreements. Provided copy with PIC. Discussed need for all food handling employees (every staff member at facility) to sign the document and understand the contents. Explained document to PIC. Inspector will follow-up on 5/25/21.

findings.title: Procedures for responding to vomiting and diarrheal events
findings.comment:
2-501.11: A FOOD ESTABLISHMENT shall have written procedures for EMPLOYEES to follow when responding to vomiting or diarrheal events that involve the discharge of vomitus or fecal matter onto surfaces in the FOOD ESTABLISHMENT. The procedures shall address the specific actions EMPLOYEES must take to minimize the spread of contamination and the exposure of EMPLOYEES, consumers, FOOD, and surfaces to vomitus or fecal matter. Reference 2-501.11.  

Observed no Norovirus illness clean-up policy. Provided copy to PIC. Discussed procedure with PIC. Facility has bleach to perform procedure. COS.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-601.11: (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch. 

(REPEAT) Observed can opener blade to not be clean to sight or touch. Discussed routine cleaning with PIC - wash, rinse, and sanitize. Can opener was taken away for cleaning. COS. This is a repeat violation since the last routine inspection on 3/10/20.

Observed ice scoop at server station to be placed on top of ice machine. Place ice scoop on a surface that can be washed, rinsed, and sanitized along with ice scoop. Discussed changing practice with PIC. Ice scoop was taken for wash, rinse, and sanitizing. COS.

findings.title: Proper hot holding temperatures
findings.comment:
3-501.16: (A) (1) TCS FOOD shall be maintained at 135F or above. Roasts can be maintained at 130F or above. 

(REPEAT) Observed egg drop soup to be 126 degrees F - probed after mixing soup. Temperature was 87 degrees F before stirring. Time/Temperature Control for Food Safety not maintained at 135 degrees F or above. Reviewed hot holding requirements with PIC. Inadequately held food was rapidly reheated to 165 degrees F or above. Soup was prepared within the hour per PIC. COS. This is a repeat violation since the last routine inspection on 3/10/20.

findings.title: Toxic substances properly identified, stored, and used
findings.comment:
7-102.11: Working containers used for storing POISONOUS OR TOXIC MATERIALS such as cleaners and SANITIZERS taken from bulk supplies shall be clearly and individually identified with the common name of the material. 

Observed two unlabeled spray bottles. PIC labeled each bottle upon request. Spray cleaner and alcohol were in bottles. Label with common name of material. COS.

findings.title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control
findings.comment:
3-501.15: (A) Cooling shall be accomplished with time and temperature criteria by using following methods: FOOD in shallow pans, Separating FOOD into small portions, using rapid cooling EQUIPMENT, stirring food in container placed in ice bath, containers facilitating heat transfer, adding ice, other effective methods. P (B) When placed in cooling or cold holding EQUIPMENT, FOOD containers shall be: arranged to maximize heat transfer through container walls, loosely covered or uncovered, and during cooling period. C

(REPEAT) Observed method of cooking to be inadequate - time is not documented for cooling. Discussed HACCP concept with PIC. Add time to foods that are cooling - soups, chicken placed in ice bath. This is a repeat violation since the last routine inspection on 3/10/20.

findings.title: Thermometers provided & accurate
findings.comment:
4-302.12: (A) FOOD TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICES shall be provided and readily accessible for use in ensuring attainment and maintenance of FOOD temperatures. (B) A TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICE with a suitable small diameter probe that is designed to measure the temperature of thin masses shall be provided and readily accessible to accurately measure the temperature in thin FOODS such as MEAT patties and FISH filets. 

Observed no probe thermometer at facility. Purchase a probe thermometer to measure the temperature of foods. Calibrate as needed. Inspector will follow-up on 5/25/21.

findings.title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display
findings.comment:
3-305.11: (A) FOOD shall be protected from contamination: In clean dry location, not exposed to any form of contamination, at least 6 inches above floor. (B) FOOD in working containers and packages may be stored less than 6 inches on case lot handling EQUIPMENT. (C) Pressurized BEVERAGE containers, cased FOOD in waterproof containers, and milk containers in plastic crates may be stored on floor. 

Observed multiple areas where food items were not at least 6 inches off the floor - walk-in freezer boxes, sugar bags, boxes with canned food, rice bags, dried chili bags. Ensure all food items are at least 6 inches off the floor throughout facility.

findings.title: Wiping cloths: properly used and stored
findings.comment:
3-304.14: (A) Cloths in-use for wiping FOOD spills for TABLEWARE and carryout containers shall be dry and used for no other purpose. (B) Cloths in-use for wiping counters and EQUIPMENT surfaces shall be held between uses in chemical sanitizer at proper solution and laundered daily. (C) Cloths in-use for wiping raw animal FOOD surfaces shall be separate from other cloths. (D) Dry wiping cloths and sanitizing solution shall be free of FOOD debris and other soil. (E) Containers of sanitizing solution shall be stored off floor and used in manner to prevent contamination. (F) SINGLE-USE disposable sanitizer wipes shall be used in accordance with EPA labels. 

(REPEAT) Observed multiple in-use rags at bar and throughout kitchen to not be immersed in sanitizer. Wet rags were on countertops. Discussed need for a sanitizer bucket with appropriate concentration and in-use rags held within sanitizer at all times - change sanitizer as needed when concentration runs low. This is a repeat violation since the last routine inspection on 3/10/20.

findings.title: Utensils, equipment & linens: properly stored, dried, & handled
findings.comment:
4-904.11: (A) cleaned and SANITIZED UTENSILS shall be handled, displayed, and dispensed to prevent FOOD- and lip-contact surface contamination. (B) UTENSILS not prewrapped shall be presented so only handles are touched by EMPLOYEES and/or CONSUMERS. (C) SINGLE-SERVCIE ARTICLES intended for FOOD- and lip-contact shall be furnished for CONSUMER with wrapper or APPROVED dispenser. 

Observed multiple areas throughout facility to have plates and bowls not inverted - no protection from cross contamination. Flip plates and bowls in order to have the food- and lip-contact surfaces covered and free from cross contamination. Observed two bowls of spoons at the bar area where spoons had food- and lip-contact surfaces mixed with spoons that handles were upright. Keep all spoons in bowl with handles upright - prevention from cross contamination. Discussed with PIC. Cease practices.

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, & used; test strips
findings.comment:
4-303.11: (A) Cleaning agents used to clean EQUIPMENT shall be provided and available during all hours of operation. (B) Chemical SANITIZERS shall be provided and available during all hours of operation. 

Observed no sanitization buckets throughout facility. In-use rags were on counters with no form of sanitization buckets. Facility must have multiple sanitization buckets provided and available during all hours of operation. Ensure employee's are frequently making sanitization buckets and changing as needed. Keep in-use rags in buckets at all times. Use test strips to maintain concentration accuracy. Inspector will follow-up on 5/25/21.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
4-601.11: (B) The FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of cooking EQUIPMENT and pans shall be kept free of encrusted grease deposits and other soil accumulations. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

Observed the following areas that were dusty or had dirt and debris:
1. Walk-in freezer fans - dust accumulation
2. Tin foil around rice steamer - change foil frequently
3. Hood baffles covered with grime and debris
4. Warmers in front of prep coolers - dust under warmers on grates
5. Walk-in cooler fans - dust accumulation

Ensure routine cleaning of facility - wash, rinse, and sanitize the above areas before next routine inspection.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
6-201.11: Except as specified under § 6-201.14 and except for antislip floor coverings or applications that may be used for safety reasons, floors, floor coverings, walls, wall coverings, and ceilings shall be designed, constructed, and installed so they are SMOOTH and EASILY CLEANABLE. 

Observed the following areas no longer smooth and easily cleanable:
1. Caulk at 3 compartment sink of bar - moldy - re-caulk between wall and 3 compartment sink at bar
2. Caulk at dish machine area - missing on right hand side between dish machine and wall; left hand side has moldy caulk - re-caulk between dish machine and wall

Discussed repairs with PIC. Ensure repairs are conducted before next routine inspection.

findings.title: All food employees have food handler training
findings.comment:
410 ILCS 625 and IAC Section 750.3430 (C) Facility is not in compliance with the food handler law. All food handlers, other than someone who has the food service sanitation manager certificate, shall receive or obtain training in basic food handling principles as outlined in Subpart M of the Illinois Food Code. Food handlers working at a temporary food establishment are exempt from this requirement.  

Observed no food handlers licenses available during inspection. Discussed need for all employees who are NOT certified food protection manager's (CFPM's) to have food handlers licenses. Keep copies of licenses at facility in folder or binder. Ensure all employees have licensure before next routine inspection.

findings.title: Allergen training as required
findings.comment:
410 ILCS 625/3.07 Sec. 3.07. Allergen awareness training. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all certified food service sanitation managers employed by a restaurant must receive or obtain training in basic allergen awareness principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter.

Observed certified food protection manager's (CFPM's) to lack allergen training certification. Discussed with PIC. All CFPM's need allergen training and proof of certification. Keep copies at the facility in folder or binder. Provided copy of allergen training information. Ensure CFPM's have completed training and printed certifications before next routine inspection.
